title: Common
description: Definitions shared by the HOTL event and document schemas. Not an event itself. Identifier formats are owned by the service that assigns them, so ids are plain non-empty strings here: the registry treats any pattern change as breaking, so only formats fixed by a standard carry a pattern.

IntentId.description: Intent id assigned by intake, for example INT-0042.

IntentVersion.description: Version of the signed intent package: 1 at the first sign-off, one more per re-signed version.

RunId.description: Run id, for example RUN-0042-1; also the Temporal workflow id.

TaskId.description: Task id, unique within its run, for example T-7.

BriefId.description: Review brief id assigned by the review service, for example BRF-0107.

RuleId.description: Rule id, stable across the rule's versions.

RuleVersion.description: Version of a rule; 1 for its first version.

PlanVersion.description: Version of a run's plan; 1 for the first plan, one more per re-plan.

Attempt.description: Attempt number of a task; 1 for the first attempt.

Repo.description: Repository name as connected to HOTL, for example orders-service.

Branch.description: Git branch name, for example run/RUN-0042-1.

Commit.description: Full git commit id (SHA-1 or SHA-256, lowercase hex).

Person.description: A person known to HOTL, as named in intent packages and review briefs.

Actor.description: Who did something: a person or an agent.

kind.description: Whether a person or an agent acted.

name.description: Person name, or agent role when kind is agent.

Autonomy.description: Autonomy level: L1 propose, L2 act with veto window, L3 act and inform.

DocumentRef.description: Reference to an immutable document (intent package, plan, review brief, rule, report). Events reference documents instead of copying them in; the digest pins the exact content.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the document's exact bytes, lowercase hex.

Problem.description: One reason a document was rejected.

part.description: The part that failed its check: a front matter field or section name.

message.description: What is wrong, written for the person who has to fix it.

BriefCategory.description: Review brief category; decides routing and the default at the deadline.

Recipient.description: Who a brief is routed to.

kind.description: What kind of recipient name is.

name.description: Role, person or group name, for example architects.

Channel.description: Delivery channel, for example portal, slack, teams, email or inbox.

Severity.description: Hard rules block; soft rules warn.

RuleScope.description: Where a rule applies. Every listed dimension must match; an absent dimension matches everything.

repos.description: Repos the rule applies to; empty or absent means all.

layers.description: Architecture layers the rule applies to.

paths.description: File glob patterns the rule applies to.

Budget.description: Kind of budget: tokens, or wall-clock seconds.

ScopeVersion.description: Version of a run's scope: 1 for the first proposal, one more per proposal after it (a re-scope, a correction, a re-signed intent).

Confidence.description: How sure the scoper is, from 0 to 1.

ScopeEvidence.description: A knowledge graph node that shows why a repo is in a scope: a package, endpoint, event, topic, symbol, module or document the intent affects (ADR 0018).

node.description: The node's key in the knowledge graph, for example pkg:github.com/HumanOnLoop/playground/internal/api or endpoint:playground:GET /version.

label.description: The node's label, for example Package, Endpoint, Event, Topic, Symbol, Module or ADR.

commit.description: The commit the node was harvested at, as the knowledge graph records it; absent for nodes from run history.

note.description: What the node shows, in a sentence.

ScopeRepo.description: An existing repo in a scope.

reason.description: Why the intent needs a change in this repo.

evidence.description: Graph nodes that show it; the agent runtime keeps only nodes the knowledge graph has, with the graph's own commit.

hinted.description: True when the intent package hinted at this repo.

DraftProfile.description: A first sketch of a new repo's profile (documents/repo-profile.schema.json): enough to create its skeleton. The onboarder proposes the real profile once the repo exists, and the architect approves it.

languages.description: Languages of the repo, for example go or python.

image.description: The toolchain image catalogue entry its Jobs would run, for example go.

ScopeNewRepo.description: A repo the scope needs that does not exist yet. Only an architect can approve one (ADR 0018).

name.description: The new repo's name in the HOTL organisation: lower case letters, digits and hyphens.

purpose.description: What the repo is for, in a sentence or two.

technology.description: Its technology, for example go or python; picks the skeleton it is created with.

ScopeBoundary.description: A rule-protected boundary a scope crosses: a boundary rule whose condition the scope meets.

repos.description: The scope's repos that meet the rule's condition.

reason.description: How the scope meets the rule's condition.

ScopeHint.description: What the scoper made of one of the intent package's repo hints.

verdict.description: confirmed: the hint is in the scope; corrected: the evidence points elsewhere, so it is not; unknown: the graph has nothing on it.

Scope.description: Which repos a run touches, decided by the scoper from the knowledge graph before planning (ADR 0018).

summary.description: The scope in a few sentences: the components, endpoints and channels the intent affects.

newRepos.description: Repos the run needs that do not exist yet.

hints.description: One entry per repo hint of the intent package.
